DONE THIS PASS: the run calendar moved (ten holidays and three missed runs, 98 runs, lines per run 149 to 630 at sd 108 against the old 222 to 304 at sd 17) after the conventions were pinned; A3 re-routed so its monthly figure needs the ledger join, with two primaries on it, a scope device (plan 4.4's revenue sample of seventeen rows on the same working paper, own cost centres, own ledger prefix, counted in no month, separation asserted by count) and a clock device (the paper carries the run's release date from the run log, the ledger the date of the run that paid the line, differing for the seven runs released past midnight, two of which cross a month end); the dictionary made truthful about both dates; the month pinned to the month of payment; verify.py reading both samples on its own code path. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS: neither device moved the cracker, because a device a careful reader resolves from a column description cannot suppress it. The scope device is found by the unmatched-join sweep, a battery check; the clock device is resolved by reading two honest date definitions. Both are legitimate mirror devices and that is why the leakage fell from 51.2 to 26.8 while the cracker stayed at 41 of 41. OPEN: a primary per ask that is discoverable only from an internal inconsistency nothing invites.
